title: Private VPC Discovery - Hightide Logistics
summary: Discovery call to understand Hightide Logistics' requirements for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood: networking topology (VPC peering vs private endpoint), region/residency constraints across EU/US, KMS integration, SOC2/audit needs, expected throughput and latency, and next steps to scope pilot and security review.

Customer to provide VPC CIDR ranges and preferred regions (Sam) by 2026-09-28
Schedule security deep-dive with customer secops and Redwood security (Maya) week of 2026-09-28

Sam Patel: Share VPC CIDR blocks, VPC peering constraints, and CI/CD egress IPs for firewall whitelisting (due: 2026-09-28)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Time: 16:00 PDT (52 minutes)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Victor Ramos (Redwood SE), Sam Patel (Hightide Head of Infra), Laura Kim (Hightide SecEng), Derek Osei (Hightide CTO)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro  I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Victor is our SE. we mostly want to understand your constraints for a private deployment into your VPC.
[00:18] Sam Patel: Thanks. quick background: Hightide runs global logistics with regional apps in us-west, us-east, and eu-west. We have strict data residency for EU shipments. We're exploring Redwood Private because we want the model serving inside our VPC for PII and contractual reasons.
[00:36] Victor Ramos: Great. can I ask about network preferences? do you prefer VPC peering (Redwood-managed VPC peering into our VPC) or private endpoints (private link or interface endpoints)? Both have tradeoffs.
[00:51] Laura Kim: Ideally private endpoints  we prefer not to open peering across accounts because of our routing policies. We'll need private endpoint IPs/ENIs and a static set of egress IPs for firewall rules.
[01:06] Derek Osei: Also curious about cross-region: some workloads must remain in eu-west; others in us-east. Can Redwood support multiple private deployments with regional isolation?
[01:19] Victor Ramos: Yes  Redwood Private can be deployed per-region. typically we propose a control plane that is either hosted (Redwood control plane) with private connectivity or a customer-managed control plane. For strict air-gapped or on-prem you can run a private control plane. For VPC scenarios we support private endpoints per region and we can pin model inference to a region.
[01:41] Sam Patel: Ok. two things: 1) compliance  SOC2, ISO docs, audit logs, and 2) KMS. we must use our KMS for key material; no redwood-managed keys. is BYOK supported?
[01:56] Maya Chen: Yes, BYOK is supported. we integrate with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS APIs depending on your provider. we'll surface the key usage in audit logs. We'll share the security integration docs after the call.
[02:11] Laura Kim: What's the network path for inference requests? we want to know latency, and how KV cache or batching works over private connectivity.
[02:21] Victor Ramos: good question. if you use private endpoints in-region, the traffic stays within your VPC and the Redwood serving runtime runs in that same region  KV cache and batching operate locally on the same instance pool, so added latency is negligible compared to public endpoints. If you choose cross-region fallback, you'll see additional RTTs.
[02:41] Sam Patel: any specifics on required subnets, security groups, NAT? we use private subnets with NAT gateways for outbound.
[02:49] Victor Ramos: We require an app subnet for the inference cluster (private) and a set of ENIs for private interface endpoints. Outbound egress for control-plane callbacks can go over a NAT; alternatively, we can set up an egress-only configuration with whitelisted IPs. We'll provide exact port lists and CIDR recommendations in the checklist.
[03:08] Derek Osei: What about scaling and autoscaling? If traffic spikes during peak delivery hours, will the cluster autoscale within our VPC?
[03:18] Victor Ramos: Yes  our operator can scale worker nodes within your VPC using your autoscaling groups or by provisioning new instances if you give us permission. We use a horizontal scaling approach with GPU autoscaling policies. There are burst policies for capacity spikes  we can negotiate reserved capacity if you prefer predictable latency.
[03:35] Laura Kim: Are you able to support private peering to our cloud provider in cases where we use dedicated hosts? For procurement reasons we might prefer dedicated host pools.
[03:44] Maya Chen: We have two common patterns: Redwood-managed dedicated pools that sit in a customer VPC (we still manage the instances but the network is customer-owned), or a customer-managed deployment where you own the infra and we provide operators/tools. Dedicated hosts are doable; we just need instance profile/role details.
[04:02] Sam Patel: latency SLAs  do you commit to SLOs for p95 latency for generation? we have hard limits for real-time tracking features.
[04:10] Maya Chen: For Dedicated/Private deployments we can commit to SLO bands in contracts. p95 depends on model and sequence length; for smaller prompt sizes we typically see sub-200ms p95 on optimized GPUs. We'll need to run a benchmark in your environment to give concrete numbers.
[04:28] Derek Osei: Benchmarks  great. we'd like to run a short pilot (2 weeks) with a production-like trace. what's involved?
[04:36] Victor Ramos: Pilot flow: provisioning (network + infra), model onboarding, run a synthetic and recorded traffic benchmark, tune batching/quantization, then production smoke tests. Usually takes 2-4 weeks end-to-end. For VPC pilot we'll need your CIDRs and a small set of test instances.
[04:55] Laura Kim: Regarding KMS again: if the model weights are encrypted at rest with our KMS, how do you handle key access for model loads and checkpoints?
[05:05] Victor Ramos: We support encryption-at-rest using customer KMS. the serving runtime will pull keys via the KMS API and decrypt in-memory; keys are never persisted to Redwood-managed services. We can also integrate with HSM for stricter requirements.
[05:19] Sam Patel: Firewalls: we enforce very strict egress whitelisting. will you give us a fixed set of IPs for control-plane callbacks and model downloads?
[05:28] Maya Chen: Yes  for private endpoints we'll provide a set of static egress IPs for the control/data plane, and a periodic list of IPs used by our managed services. if you run customer-managed infra, you control egress.
[05:40] Derek Osei: How about observability? we need token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[05:48] Victor Ramos: We can forward audit logs to your S3/Cloud Storage or direct into your SIEM via secure syslog/SQS/Kinesis. Token-level cost extrapolation is available in the console, and we can export detailed logs for billing reconciliation.
[06:05] Sam Patel: region constraints  EU data must not leave eu-west. Can you guarantee that models used for EU are provisioned only in eu-west?
[06:14] Maya Chen: Yes  we support per-customer region pinning for model serving. We'll architect separate instance pools per-region and ensure routing policies honor residency.
[06:24] Laura Kim: Do you support private connectivity across our multiple accounts? we have a hub-and-spoke networking model.
[06:31] Victor Ramos: We typically integrate either into a spoke VPC or via private link endpoints into a centralized transit VPC. We'll work with your network team to map the hub-and-spoke. If you need cross-account endpoint creation, we can provide CloudFormation/Terraform modules.
[06:49] Sam Patel: any gotchas customers frequently run into?
[06:53] Victor Ramos: Common items: overlapping CIDRs, missing route propagation on peering, MTU issues with tunnels, and forgetting to whitelist control-plane egress. Also, some customers underestimate the test traffic needed to tune batching.
[07:08] Derek Osei: Ok. procurement and timeline: we want to go to procurement next month and have pilots running by mid-october. is that doable?
[07:17] Maya Chen: Yes. Typical timeline: security review + network checklist (1-2 weeks), procurement/legal (2-4 weeks depending on enterprise), then provisioning and pilot (2-4 weeks). If procurement moves quickly we can hit mid-october for a pilot.
[07:30] Laura Kim: We'll need SOC2 and ISO docs up front and a security deep-dive.
[07:34] Maya Chen: Absolutely. I'll coordinate the security deep-dive. Victor will also send the network checklist and sample Terraform.
[07:42] Sam Patel: One more question: model updates and rollouts  how do you handle rollback in a private deployment if a model causes regressions?
[07:49] Victor Ramos: We support canary rollouts and A/B policies in private deployments; rollback is orchestrated by the operator. We also keep previous model artifacts so you can pin versions. For strict change control we can require manual approve for rollouts.
[08:02] Derek Osei: Great. what about metrics export? we need to ship latency and error metrics to our prometheus/grafana stacks.
[08:10] Victor Ramos: We can export metrics to your Prometheus pushgateway or provide a Prometheus scrape endpoint inside the VPC for your monitoring. We also have dashboards in the Redwood console.
[08:20] Sam Patel: network egress costs  if we host in eu-west and you pull models from a central repo, will there be cross-region data transfer costs?
[08:28] Maya Chen: If we replicate model artifacts per-region, we can avoid cross-region downloads. we'll factor replication into the deployment. Model pulling can be localized to avoid egress charges.
[08:39] Laura Kim: Anything we should watch in the legal contract re: data residency and logs?
[08:45] Maya Chen: We'll include clauses for data residency, customer-managed keys, and audit log retention. We can also add an MSA addendum for private deployments specifying uptime and support SLAs.
[08:56] Sam Patel: Ok let's recap and assign owners.
[09:00] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood to send network checklist, terraform snippets, security pack and SOC2/ISO docs (Victor + Maya) by 2026-09-24. 2) Hightide to send CIDR blocks, preferred regions, and list of compliance documents (Sam + Laura) by 2026-09-28. 3) Schedule security deep-dive w/ SecOps week of 2026-09-28. 4) Plan pilot for mid-october, duration ~2 weeks.
[09:32] Derek Osei: sounds good. Laura will coordinate the secops side and procurement.
[09:36] Maya Chen: Great. i'll follow up in email and add calendar invites. Thanks everyone.
[09:43] Laura Kim: thanks all.
